name: Singapore 🇸🇬
subtitle: The island nation where hawker stalls have Michelin stars
items: Odette (Julien Royer, National Gallery, 3-star — World's 50 Best, Singapore's finest)
Burnt Ends (Dave Pynt, Teck Chye Terrace, Australian-style BBQ — queue at 6am for reservations)
Candlenut (Dempsey, Malcolm Lee, 1-star — the only Peranakan restaurant with a Michelin star)
Hawker Chan (Chinatown, Chan Hon Meng, 1-star — cheapest Michelin meal on earth, soya chicken rice)
National Kitchen by Violet Oon (National Gallery, Peranakan — the classic)
Waku Ghin (Marina Bay Sands, Tetsuya Wakuda, 2-star — book months ahead)
Thevar (Keong Saik, Mano Thevar, 1-star — modern South Indian)
Meta (Club Street, Sun Kim, 1-star — Korean-European)
Jumbo Seafood (East Coast, Clarke Quay — chilli crab, the dish you have to eat)
328 Katong Laksa (East Coast Road, the laksa benchmark)
Maxwell Food Centre (Tanjong Pagar — hawker complex, Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice)
Lau Pa Sat (CBD, Victorian cast-iron market — satay street at night)
Tiong Bahru Bakery (multiple, French-Japanese croissants)
Luke's Oyster Bar & Chop House (Gemmill Lane, East Coast)
Labrador Kitchen (Labrador Park, relaxed seafood)
Ya Kun Kaya Toast (multiple, kaya toast + half-boiled eggs — Singaporean breakfast ritual)
Hajjah Maimunah (Jalan Pisang, Malay — nasi padang institution)
Saveur (multiple, affordable French-Asian)
Smith Street Taps (Chinatown Complex, natural wine + hawker)
Michelin Guide Singapore street food stalls (the whole category is worth researching)
